title: Atomic structure & isotopes
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: What is the difference between an atom and an isotope?
How do protons, neutrons, and electrons affect an atom?
Can you explain why isotopes have the same element symbol?

explain.say: Say the three particles found in an atom.
Say where the protons and neutrons are located.
Say where the electrons are found in the atom.
Say that the number of protons defines the element.
Say that isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons.
Say that carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon.

faq.q: Why do isotopes have the same element symbol?
faq.a: They have the same number of protons, and the number of protons determines the element's identity. You might also ask: What makes them the same element? Or: How do I know they are the same element?
asks: Does the mass number change the element?

faq.q: Do electrons affect the element's identity?
faq.a: No, the number of protons determines the element. Electrons can be lost or gained, but they do not change what the element is. You could also ask: What about ions? Or: Is the charge important?
asks: Can I change the element by adding electrons?

faq.q: What is the difference between mass number and atomic number?
faq.a: The atomic number is the number of protons. The mass number is the total count of protons plus neutrons. You could also ask: How do I calculate the mass number? Or: Is the mass number always the same as the number of protons?
asks: What is the total number of particles?
How do I find the mass number?

faq.q: Can an atom have more than one type of isotope?
faq.a: Yes, an element can have many isotopes, just by changing the number of neutrons. For example, bromine has two common isotopes. You might also ask: Are all isotopes stable? Or: How many isotopes can an element have?
asks: Is it possible for one element to have many forms?
What is the most common isotope?

faq.q: Are protons and electrons equally charged?
faq.a: No, protons are positively charged, and electrons are negatively charged. They are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign. You might also ask: What is the overall charge of a neutral atom? Or: Do they balance out?
asks: What is the charge on an electron?
What is the charge on a proton?

facts: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.
Protons have a positive electrical charge.
Electrons orbit the nucleus and have a negative charge.
Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons.

quiz.say: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
quiz.why: The mass number is the total count of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

wrong.0: This only counts the protons, forgetting the neutrons.
wrong.1: This only counts the neutrons, forgetting the protons.
wrong.2: This incorrectly subtracts the number of protons from the neutrons.

quiz.say: Which particle determines the element type?
quiz.why: The number of protons is the unique identifier for any element.

wrong.0: Changing neutrons only creates an isotope, not a new element.
wrong.1: Electrons can be gained or lost without changing the element.
wrong.2: Mass number is a measurement, not a particle type.

quiz.say: If an atom has 8 protons and 10 neutrons, what is its isotope name?
quiz.why: It has 8 protons, so it is Oxygen, and 8 plus 2 neutrons gives a mass of 18.

wrong.0: This is the most common isotope, but the question specified 10 neutrons.
wrong.1: This changes the number of protons, making it a different element.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the mass number by only counting the neutrons.
